summary.short: Amends Virginia Code § 18.2-374.1 on child pornography. Defines the offense, covers depictions where the minor need not actually exist, allows age to be inferred from appearance, sets prison terms and mandatory minimums by victim age, and sets venue. The provided text states no effective date.
summary.long: The act amends and reenacts § 18.2-374.1 of the Code of Virginia on child pornography. Subsection A defines child pornography as sexually explicit visual material that utilizes or has as a subject an identifiable minor, or that depicts a minor in nudity or sexual conduct where obscene; for the second limb the minor depicted need not actually exist. Sexually explicit visual material includes digital images and cached images when three or more are present. Subsection B lists production-related offenses (enticing a person under 18, producing, knowingly participating in production, and knowingly financing), with subsections B1 and B5 repealed. Subsections C1 and C2 set prison terms by the age of the subject (under 15: five to 30 years; 15 to under 18: one to 20 years), with higher mandatory minimums where the offender is at least seven years older and longer terms for second or subsequent violations. C3 requires mandatory minimum terms to run consecutively with any other sentence. Subsection D allows inference of minority from text, title or appearance. Subsection E sets venue. Section 2 states that the act may increase periods of imprisonment and that the Virginia Criminal Sentencing Commission must assign a minimum fiscal impact of $50,000.

events.note: The text gives no dated events for this instrument. It has no enactment, signature, effective-date or sunset provision, and no relative or conditional start date. The 2023 Special Session I Acts cited in section 2 are another act's history and are not coded as events here.

obligations.note: The bill amends the criminal child pornography offence and penalty provisions of Va. Code § 18.2-374.1. Its offence list (B), mandatory minimum penalties (C1-C3), inference rule (D) and venue rule (E) are enforcement or evidentiary provisions, not duties. The definitions in A impose no duty. Section 2 is a fiscal-impact statement that restates an existing Chapter 1 requirement, not a new duty.
